baseline.name: Bottom-up linked-list merge sort
baseline.approach: Repeatedly merge adjacent runs of doubling length by relinking nodes.
baseline.space: O(1) auxiliary for an iterative bottom-up implementation

archived.name: Insertion into a sorted list prefix
archived.time: O(n^2) worst case; O(n) when each next node inserts immediately at the front
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary space; existing list nodes are relinked

why: Insertion sort is direct and can be linear when each next node belongs at the front, but it repeatedly rescans long sorted prefixes on other inputs.
quantitative_comparison: For ascending distinct input, this source performs 1+2+...+(n-1)=n(n-1)/2 value comparisons. Bottom-up merging has O(n log n) comparison growth. No general improvement over merge sort is supported.
tradeoffs: Both can reuse nodes. This insertion implementation is also not stable for equal values, while a merge sort can preserve their order.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
